slots.label: linear-growth misconception
slots.description: A fixed annual rate means the same dollar amount is added every year.
slots.repair: A fixed percent is applied to a changing balance, so the dollar amount can grow.
slots.repairQuestion: After the first $50 is added, what balance earns interest in the next year?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner says the next period uses the updated balance or that the dollar interest can increase because the base increased.

slots.label: principal-only misconception
slots.description: Compound interest is just interest on the original principal.
slots.repair: That describes simple interest. Compound interest includes accumulated interest in the future base.
slots.repairQuestion: What part besides the original principal can earn interest in compound interest?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner identifies accumulated or previous interest as also earning interest.

slots.label: frequency-does-not-matter misconception
slots.description: Compounding frequency is irrelevant if the annual rate is the same.
slots.repair: With the same nominal annual rate, more frequent compounding updates the balance more often, changing the amount unless the rate is already expressed as an effective annual yield.
slots.repairQuestion: Why might monthly compounding produce a different balance than annual compounding at the same nominal rate?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner says the balance is updated more often or the rate is applied across more periods.

slots.text: Compound interest is interest on the original principal plus accumulated interest. Each compounding period updates the balance, so growth is multiplicative rather than a fixed linear dollar add-on. Simple interest uses only the original principal; compound interest uses the growing balance.
